text: Imran Shafiq, a student with a declared monthly income of PKR 20,000, exhibited classic money mule behavior between June 1 and June 10, 2026. The account received 21 inbound transfers totaling approximately PKR 1,041,000 from 15 distinct counterparties, including Talha Latif, Rabia Khalid, and Fatima Zafar, via IBFT channels. This volume is significantly disproportionate to his declared income and student status. The funds were rapidly swept out of the account through two large wallet transfers to QuickPay wallet ***0932 (PKR 121,000 on June 4 and PKR 319,000 on June 9) and two high-value ATM withdrawals at an ATM in Islamabad (PKR 286,000 on June 5 and PKR 263,000 on June 10). The pattern of receiving numerous small-to-medium transfers from unrelated individuals and immediately moving the aggregate value to cash or digital wallets is indicative of layering activities associated with money laundering. The geographic discrepancy between the customer’s residence in Karachi and the ATM withdrawals in Islamabad further heightens the suspicion. No legitimate business or personal reason for this activity has been identified, warranting the filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report.
